title: Several Distribution Reward Instances are Active while lacking a payment address or even a tracking methodology
content:
DeFi Saver, CoW Swap and Yearn (Gimme) each publish a concrete partner payment address (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.3.3.5.0.6.2, .4.3.5.0.6.2, .6.3.5.0.6.2). ParaSwap, MOM and Lazy Summer Protocol instead read: "The payment address of this Third Party Partner will be defined in a future iteration of the Skybase Artifact."

Lazy Summer Protocol goes further. Its Tracking Methodology (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.8.1.2) is simply "This parameter will be defined in a future iteration of the Skybase Artifact" — while the Instance sits in the Active Instances Directory with a Reward Code of `1016` already assigned.

This exposes what `Active` actually certifies. It marks a relationship as invoked and governed, not as operational: an Active Instance may currently have no rule for measuring the demand it rewards and no address to pay it to. Attribution and settlement can be filled in after the Instance goes live.

The tension is with the Instance's own logic. The reward program's integrity rests on the Reward Code + Tracking Methodology pair, and an Instance missing the methodology has a code that counts nothing. If rewards accrue in the interim, the amount owed is being determined by a rule that will be written later — and written through a route that, for these Active Data and parameter documents, does not necessarily involve a token holder vote.

Read charitably, this is the same pattern as the deferred Genesis Supply: the Atlas prefers to register a real relationship with acknowledged gaps over keeping it off the record until complete. The cost is that "Active" cannot be read as "fully specified."
description: ParaSwap, MOM and Lazy Summer Protocol have payment addresses deferred to a future Artifact iteration, and Lazy Summer's Tracking Methodology is undefined — yet all three are live Instances.
